answers.Q-1:
Control characters are ASCII bytes 0x00-0x1F and 0x7F. These are the standard control characters
in ASCII. All of them should be rejected to prevent non-printable characters in the input.
answers.Q-2:
Whitespace includes all characters that Python's str.isspace() returns True for: space (0x20),
tab (0x09), newline (0x0A), carriage return (0x0D), form feed (0x0C), vertical tab (0x0B),
and other Unicode whitespace characters. All should be rejected.
answers.Q-3:
For str input, validate the characters as str before encoding to bytes. This catches invalid
characters at the string level and is more precise than post-conversion validation.
answers.Q-4:
Reject input with more than two trailing '=' characters as invalid. Base64 allows 0, 1, or 2
padding characters; anything more is malformed.
answers.Q-5:
Empty input (both b'' and '') is valid base64 and should decode to b'' without raising an error.
It represents zero bytes of data.
answers.Q-6:
Always raise BadData for invalid alphabet characters, including in signature contexts. BadData
is the appropriate exception for malformed input; it should be raised consistently.

answers.Q-1:
Input containing invalid characters ('+', '/', whitespace, non-ASCII, control chars, or '=' outside end) raises BadData exception for both str and bytes inputs.
A signed value or serialized token that has been modified with inserted characters outside the alphabet is rejected during verification.
Running python -m pytest -q produces all passing tests, including new tests covering the stricter validation behavior.
answers.Q-2:
Function: base64_decode(s: Union[str, bytes]) -> bytes
Input: string or bytes in URL-safe base64 format, potentially with up to 2 trailing '=' padding characters
Output: decoded bytes
Invalid input: raises BadData exception instead of silently discarding invalid characters
answers.Q-3:
Valid alphabet: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '-', '_' (41 characters)
Padding boundary: 0, 1, or 2 trailing '=' characters accepted; '=' anywhere else is invalid
Any character outside this set (including '+', '/', whitespace, non-ASCII, control chars) is a boundary violation
answers.Q-4: BadData exception raised for any of: '+' character, '/' character, whitespace (space/tab/newline), non-ASCII characters, control characters, '=' padding in middle or more than 2 at end
answers.Q-5:
Validate each input character against the URL-safe base64 alphabet (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '-', '_', and '=' at end only)
Raise BadData when validation fails
Accept unpadded input and input with 1-2 trailing '=' characters
Reject altered signatures by detecting inserted invalid characters
Maintain existing test coverage and behavior for valid inputs
answers.Q-6:
Changing the public function signatures of base64_decode or base64_encode
Adding new package dependencies
Modifying the encoding algorithm itself
Changing how signature generation works (only stricter decoding/validation)
Supporting non-URL-safe base64 formats
answers.Q-7:

Performance: No significant degradation in decode speed (measurable by existing test execution time remaining reasonable)
Compatibility: All existing tests pass without modification (measurable by test suite success)
